newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Drop in BTA unjustified - Champalimaud.
newsitem.headline: Drop in BTA unjustified - Champalimaud.

text.p: The drop in the share price of Banco Totta e Acores (BTA) is not justified and sellers of the paper could lose money, majority shareholder Antonio Champalimaud said.
Champalimaud told Reuters he planned to propose to the bank's general assembly a "substantially superior" dividend for 1996 than the announced 135 escudos per share.
BTA shares dropped to around 2,700 escudos per share this morning from Friday's close of 3,030 escudos after the bank announced a lower than expected dividend for 1996 of 135 escudos per share.
The market had expected a dividend of 190 escudos, identical to the 1995 level.
BTA stood at 2,740 escudos, down 290, in volume of 626,173 shares at 1355 GMT.
"This (drop in BTA share price) is too much and is not in any way justified. There is no reason for this," Champalimaud said.
"My feeling is that whoever bets on this (fall in BTA share price) will lose (money)," he said.

Champalimaud's son Luis, who took over the presidency of BTA from Alipio Dias on Friday, announced that the 1996 dividend would stand at 135 escudos and that 1996 net consolidated profit would be 15 billion escudos, down from 17.2 billion in 1995.

Antonio Champalimaud said: "I will go the the general assembly and, if the low dividend is still on the cards, I will call for a dividend that is substantially superior to the number that is seen as probable (135 escudos)."
